Pyrethrum is rapidly toxic to many insects. It has a much quicker knock-down effect than clofenotane or lin- dane, but it is less persistent and less stable. Its action can be en- hanced by certain substances such as piperonyl butoxide (p.2049), and pyrethrins with piperonyl butoxide are used clini- cally in the treatment of pediculosis (p.2034). Pyrethroid insecticides (synthetic analogues of pyrethrins), such as permethrin and phenothrin, are also used clinically; deltame- thrin and permethrin are among those used for the vector control of malaria. Pyrethrum, pyrethrins, and pyrethroids are also used as topical ectoparasiticides in veterinary practice and as agricultural, horti- cultural, and household insecticides.
